title: Review (Supported): on fresh seeds 7-8 swarm-chemistry recipe 3/18 bodies split ~60 times per 3000 steps and re-fuse (1-2 persistent splits, 64-67 merges), with a real blue outer layer (blue share 0.20-0.24 in the core, 0.47-0.52 at the edge)
summary: c16's body18.py (recipe 3/18, 1200 agents, periodic 1400^2, uniform random start, 3000 steps) on seeds 7 and 8: 1-5 bodies at a time (mean 1.88/1.90), splits 64/60, persistent over 400 steps 1/2, merges 67/64. Radial composition after t=500: blue 0.239/0.234 at the centre and 0.472/0.515 in the outermost bin; red 0.35-0.38 -> 0.29/0.25; green 0.41-0.44 -> 0.24/0.23. A labkit run of the world the finding names (the 2-species sighting world, seed 7): 10-23 components, 1 split, 0 persistent, 8 merges. Both runs agree with the finding: layered bodies, no lineage.

observations.D: body18/b18_s7.json, b18_s8.json: splits 64/60, persistent 1/2, merges 67/64 (negative replicated); blue share 0.23-0.24 core -> 0.47-0.52 edge

controls_run.D: body18 persistence criterion (daughters in different bodies 400 steps later) on 2 fresh seeds; labkit_world/seed7 for the named world

verdicts.limitation: The finding's world field names the 2-species sighting world while its experiment is the 3-species recipe 3/18 in body18.py; I ran both. No test of whether the blue layer does work.
